subjective.question: Describe the process of Direct Text Extraction in the System, including its primary function and how it works with scanned text.
What are the advantages of using overlapping segments when chunking text, and how does this improve question generation?
Explain the purpose of Data Cleaning in the System and how it improves the quality of generated questions.
Describe the process of selecting an LLM for question generation, including any pre-defined lists or user input involved.

context:
DOCUMENTATION 
The System is designed to work in three parts -:  
 1. Question Generation  
 2. Question Evaluation 
 3. Answer Generation 
֎ For the 1st part the process goes as-: 
i) Direct Text Extraction -:  The script uses the fitz library (PyMuPDF) to read the documents. It moves 
through every page inside the PDF and extracts the texts written inside it using .get_text(). And if 
just in case the pdf is a scanned image then OCR is embedded in the system which allows to read the 
scanned text which is uploaded. 
ii) Text Chunking -:    As the whole chapters are too large for the LLM's context window, the 
extracted text is sliced into overlapping segments. It creates chunks of 1200 characters, with a 100-
character overlap between consecutive chunks. This overlap helps ensure that sentences or 
concepts aren't abruptly cut off at the boundaries. Now if the pdf is above 1200 characters then  
instead, it processes the entire 10,000-character document by cutting it up into multiple smaller 
pieces, one after another, until it reaches the end.  
iii) Data Cleaning -:  After the text is extracted, the content may still contain irregular formatting, 
unnecessary line breaks, spacing problems, or page artifacts from the original PDF structure. The 
becomes clean. 
iv) Selection of AI Model  -:  The choice of LLM can be chosen to generate the question paper 
accordingly. 
v) Sending Context to the AI Model -: The processed educational text is converted into prompts. 
These prompts instruct the AI model about what type of question should be generated. 
For example, the system may ask the model to generate: 
+ MCQs 
+ Fill in the blanks 
+ Subjective questions 
vi) AI Understanding and Question Generation -: Inside the Transformer model the prompts 
alongwith the text which is sent from the pdf is worked out to generate the question paper of the 
type. 
vii) Cleaning Generated Questions -:  The generated questions often contains noise which needs to 
be removed. These cleaning are done to remove the unwanted symbols from the text. 
This is the whole process through which a Question Paper is generated accordingly.  
֎ Now for the 2nd part of the model where the evaluation of each question is 
done as-: 
i) Semantic Evaluation of Generated Questions -: A textbook question reference needs to uploaded 
here to match the following questions which are generated.  
ii) Matching of the questions -: The system checks whether the AI-generated questions are 
educationally similar to real textbook questions. Instead of simple keyword matching, the system 
checks the matching using four types of metric - BLEU, BERT, ROUGE, METEOR. 
ii) Metrics-: Individual metric option for each of those are present to match and check from the 
question paper and the generated questions as how much it matches.  
֎ As this is the whole raw system made. Now each LLM is finetuned 
accordingly to see how each of the LLM reacts to the question generation. The 
steps explained are -: 
i) A whole class's textbook is taken and is divided into chapters separately.  
ii) Matching the textbook's class a file is created for questions' where textbook questions (taken 
from XAM IDEA & ARIHANT) are taken in the form of MCQ and Long Answer Question and kept 
inside QUESTION folder in a json format. 
iii) Now each LLM is being fine tuned in different ranks ranging from (2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64) using the 
QLORA technique and each time the chapters and questions' are used to fine tune the LLM's. 
iv) Now after the finetuned adapters are trained and saved the adapter is need to be merged with 
the Base Model to check how well a LLM responds with the data. 
v) The llama.cpp repository is installed and it is used to convert the adapter model into GGUF Format 
as in this model Ollama is used to make question paper and Ollama's entire engine is built around 
llama.cpp, it simply cannot read PyTorch .safetensors files. It only understands GGUF. So the GGUF 
Format is required for it. 
vi) And at last a Modelfile is created due to Ollama doesn't automatically know it exists or what to do 
with it. So we can think of a Modelfile exactly like a Dockerfile for AI models. The Modelfile acts as 
the instruction manual for importing the file into that registry.
